title: Daily Morning & Evening Routines
description: Describe your everyday schedule from dawn to night using adverbs of frequency and sequence words.
objectives: Sequence daily activities using connectors (first, then, after that, finally)
Express frequency of habits using adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, never)
Position adverbs of frequency correctly before main verbs and after 'to be'

vocabularyList.definition: A cubicle or bath in which a person stands under a spray of water to wash.

The main meal of the day, taken either around midday or in the evening.

vocabularyList.definition: To clean or smooth with a brush.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Brush your teeth twice every day.

vocabularyList.definition: To go away from a place.

vocabularyList.definition: To rest from work or engage in an enjoyable activity.

vocabularyList.definition: To engage in physical activity to sustain or improve health.

sections.title: Connecting Actions & Expressing Frequency
sections.content:
To describe your daily routine smoothly, you need two linguistic tools:
1. **Adverbs of Frequency**: How often you do an action.
2. **Sequence Words**: The chronological order of your actions.

tables.title: Scale of Frequency Adverbs
rows: I always brush my teeth before bed.
We often walk in the park.
Before main verb / Start of sentence
They never arrive late for class.

tables.title: Daily Sequence Markers
rows: First, I wake up and pray.
Finally, I go to bed at ten.

callouts.title: Word Order of Frequency Adverbs
callouts.text: Put the frequency adverb **before normal action verbs** (*I **always** wake*), but **after the verb to be** (*He is **always** polite*).

callouts.title: Never Use 'Never' with 'Don't'
callouts.text: 'Never' is already negative. Never say 'I don't never go'. Say: 'I **never** go'.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Use frequency adverbs: always (100%), usually (80%), often (60%), sometimes (40%), never (0%).
Adverb position: BEFORE normal action verbs (I always pray); AFTER the verb to be (She is always kind).
Use sequence words to tell your day: First -> Then -> After that -> Finally.
Never double-negate with 'never' (say 'He never smokes', not 'doesn't never').
